zh.text: 1/ 如果新通脹目標是3%如@BillAckman建議，那麼所有名義利率必須相應上升，因為聯儲長期並不控制實際利率。因此SpaceX無論如何都將支付更高成本。

en.text: 1/ If new inflation target is 3% as @BillAckman advises then all nominal rates must rise commensurately since the Fed does not in the long run control real rates. So SpaceX is going to be paying more, regardless.

zh.text: 正是在此背景下，@billackman 的此帖得到如此回應。人們可就工業革命期間自然通脹率提出經濟論點，但在聯儲是股票上漲最大風險之時顯得方便。連結至 BillAckman 帖。

en.text: It is in that context that this post from @billackman got such a response. One could make an economic argument about the natural rate of inflation during an industrial revolution, but it seems convenient at a time when the Fed is the biggest risk to stocks going higher. Link to BillAckman post.

en.text: CHART OF THE DAY: Long Dollars $DXY Vs. Short Gold and Bitcoin Continue To Be Alpha With These Correlations via @hedgeye.

zh.text: TotalEnergies 與 Continental Resources 簽訂天然氣資產交易。TotalEnergies SE (TTE) 與油田運營商 Continental Resources 達成協議，收購天然氣上游資產權益。預計到 2032 年為 TotalEnergies 美國淨天然氣產量增加約 26,000 桶油當量每日。

en.text: TotalEnergies Inks Deal With Continental Resources for Natural Gas Assets. TotalEnergies SE (TTE) has entered into an agreement with oilfield operator Continental Resources to acquire interests in natural gas upstream assets. Expected to add roughly 26,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day to TotalEnergies' net gas production in the US by 2032.

zh.text: @JensenHuang，還不是「萬億美元人」，因為$NVDA在他回歸時只增加了9520億美元。那買回了上週約一半的慘烈跌幅。它可能修復了$SPX的損失，但不是聯準會、曲線或現金信貸。

en.text: @JensenHuang , not quite a "Trillion $ Man" as $NVDA only gained $952B on his return. That bought back about 1/2 the carnage from last week. It may have fixed the $SPX loss but not the Fed, the curve or cash credit.

zh.text: Charlie Bilello 指出 $VIX 今日下跌 26%，是歷史上第七大單日百分比跌幅。這是本月第三次 $VIX 單日下跌超過 20%。波動率的波動性極少如此高，市場從自滿迅速轉為恐懼再轉回。

en.text: Charlie Bilello notes the $VIX fell 26% today, its 7th biggest one-day percentage decline in history. This is the 3rd time this month the $VIX has fallen more than 20% in a single day. The volatility of volatility has rarely been higher, with markets swinging from complacency to fear and back again quickly.
